lines.text: | **It comes upon a person** | "dread came upon me, and trembling"; "Fear and trembling come upon me"; "fear fell upon him"; "Fear seized them all". The person is the one acted on | Job 4:14; Psa 55:5; Luk 1:12; Luk 7:16 | S |

| **It is felt in the heart and the body together** | "he was afraid, and his heart trembled greatly"; "My flesh trembles for fear of you"; "which made all my bones shake"; "fighting without and fear within" | 1Sa 28:5; Psa 119:120; Job 4:14; 2Cor 7:5 | S |
| **It has a cause outside and often a reason inside** | "I heard the sound of you in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked" | Gen 3:10 | S |

| **The nearest statement of what it is** | "There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear. For fear has to do with punishment". The verse before sets it: "so that we may have confidence for the day of judgment". This is said of fear before judgment, not of every fear (FE-136) | 1Jo 4:17–18 | S; the limit is R |

| **Named as a bondage** | "you did not receive the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear"; "through fear of death were subject to lifelong slavery"; "God gave us a spirit not of fear but of power and love and self-control" | Rom 8:15; Heb 2:15; 2Ti 1:7 | S |

| **As a standing toward God: commanded, learned, given** | "what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear the Lord your God"; "that they may hear and learn to fear the Lord your God"; "I will put the fear of me in their hearts, that they may not turn from me" | Deu 10:12; Deu 31:12; Jer 32:40 | S |

| **The fear of God, named by what it is** | "The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge"; "The fear of the Lord is hatred of evil"; "a fountain of life"; "It was a covenant of fear, and he feared me" | Pro 1:7; Pro 8:13; Pro 14:27; Mal 2:5 | S |
| **Something owed** | "If then I am a father, where is my honor? And if I am a master, where is my fear?"; "respect to whom respect is owed" | Mal 1:6; Rom 13:7 | S |

**What this shows (R):** the verses speak of fear in two ways that do not reduce to each other. In one, fear happens to a person, and the person is acted on. In the other, fear of God is a standing that is required, learned, given and owed. Exo 20:20 puts both in one sentence: "Do not fear, for God has come to test you, that the fear of him may be before you, that you may not sin" (FE-20). I note the two. No verse says they are two kinds.

| 1 | **What it is turned toward** | The same people, the same root: "they feared greatly" at Egypt; after the crossing, "the people feared the Lord, and they believed". In the boat: afraid in the storm, then "filled with great fear" and "Who then is this". "do not fear what they fear … Let him be your fear" | Exo 14:10, 31; Jon 1:5, 16; Mar 4:40–41; Isa 8:12–13 | 1, 2, 4 | S |

| 3 | **One fear taken away, another set in its place, by one speaker** | "Do not fear, for God has come to test you, that the fear of him may be before you"; "do not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul. Rather fear him"; then "Fear not, therefore; you are of more value than many sparrows" | Exo 20:20; Mat 10:28, 31 | 1, 4 | S |

| 4 | **Who speaks "fear not", and on what ground** | God: "for I am with you"; Jesus: "it is I"; an angel: "for your prayer has been heard". Jael: "do not be afraid", before the tent peg | Isa 41:10; Mat 14:27; Luk 1:13; Judg 4:18 | 1, 4 | S |

| 6 | **Where the heart is** | Fear "taught by men" while "their hearts are far from me"; fear put "in their hearts" | Isa 29:13; Jer 32:40 | 1 | S |

| 7 | **Faith and trust** | "When I am afraid, I put my trust in you"; "The fear of man lays a snare, but whoever trusts in the Lord is safe"; "Why are you so afraid? Have you still no faith?"; "By faith he left Egypt, not being afraid of the anger of the king, for he endured as seeing him who is invisible" | Psa 56:3; Pro 29:25; Mar 4:40; Heb 11:27 | 1, 2, 4 | S |

| 8 | **Love and sonship** | "perfect love casts out fear"; "you did not receive the spirit of slavery to fall back into fear, but you have received the Spirit of adoption as sons". Against these, God as father and master: "where is my honor? … where is my fear?"; "if you call on him as Father … conduct yourselves with fear" | 1Jo 4:18; Rom 8:15; Mal 1:6; 1Pe 1:17 | 1–4 | S; each verse names its own fear; Mal 1:6 states father and fear in one verse |

| 9 | **Who meets it: one event, two responses** | "When justice is done, it is a joy to the righteous but terror to evildoers"; one scroll, the officials "turned one to another in fear", "neither the king nor any of his servants who heard all these words was afraid"; "people fainting with fear" and "straighten up and raise your heads" | Pro 21:15; Jer 36:16, 24; Luk 21:26, 28 | 2, 3, 4 | S |

| 10 | **What it leads to, before the same kind of act** | "they were afraid, and they glorified God"; "asked him to depart from them, for they were seized with great fear". Rahab's dread ends "for the Lord your God, he is God"; Moab's dread ends "Come now, curse this people for me" | Mat 9:8; Luk 8:37; Jos 2:11; Num 22:6 | 3, 4 | S |

| 11 | **One's own conduct** | "rulers are not a terror to good conduct, but to bad"; "if you do wrong, be afraid"; "respect to whom respect is owed"; "I also will choose harsh treatment for them and bring their fears upon them, because when I called, no one answered" | Rom 13:3–4, 7; Isa 66:4 | 3, 4 | S |
| 12 | **Pride** | "So do not become proud, but fear"; "The horror you inspire has deceived you, and the pride of your heart" | Rom 11:20; Jer 49:16 | 3, 4 | S |

| 13 | **Who holds it, and toward whom** | A people "a horror" to those who pass by and hiss; the prophet: "dismay has taken hold on me"; Eli's "heart trembled for the ark of God"; "I am afraid that … your thoughts will be led astray" | Jer 19:8; Jer 8:21; 1Sa 4:13; 2Cor 11:3 | 2, 3, 4 | S |

- **Comparison with 10.1** (approved as a separate step, #1959). This overview is its input. The overview already shows two places where 10.1 says more than its verse: 1Jo 4:18 (FE-136) and Heb 10:31 (FE-144). The comparison would go through 10.1 *Fear* section by section against §A–§D.
- "hear and learn" is Deu 31:12, not Deu 4:10
- Jer 36:24 is "was afraid", not "were not afraid"
- Isa 66:4 is quoted in full
